authorityClass.AUTHORITATIVE: the use is a lawful current-authority access of its owning fact (exact key, exact execution fence, owner-internal monotonic counter allocation, or the owner reading its own state machine); it moves into the target owner command
authorityClass.DIAGNOSTIC: the use is presentation/telemetry only (operator lists, dashboards, logs); it may survive as a projection/diagnostic read and may never authorize a transition
authorityClass.DELETE: the use selects or mutates authority through a channel the EK target model removes (task-status scheduling, projection-derived dependency state, recency/newest-row-wins selection, MAX(id) adoption, direct writes outside the owning aggregate); EK rewrites or deletes it

disposition.retain-and-move: fact and its owning repository survive; they move to the new kernel package and protocol
disposition.rewrite: the fact or access is re-expressed (recency selection -> exact revision; direct SQL writer -> typed owning command; journal -> event+obligation)
disposition.delete: the fact, table, access path or writer is removed with its legacy composition at EK-8

accessKind.READ_DECISION: read on a production decision path (dispatch, admission, settlement, recovery, gates, effects)
accessKind.READ_PRESENTATION: read serving operator/UI/MCP query surfaces only

residualRisks: The census enumerates readers at SQL-statement granularity and attributes repository-method calls through file-level repository ownership; a call-graph-precise attribution (method -> method) would refine decision-reader lists but does not change any classification.

tracker-view/engine-supervisor.mjs and scripts/factory*.mjs are included as production operator surfaces; other scripts (testbed/bootstrap harnesses) are out of census scope and flagged as diagnostic-only tooling.

Non-SQL authority surfaces (in-memory module-level composition-root handles, process-global effect registry named by ADR-053) are not enumerable by the SQL scanner; they are carried qualitatively in the family records and must be re-audited by the EK-8 legacy-zero ratchet.

The WP-16 site lists (role resolution, prompt assembly) are believed complete for the production worker path; the conformance/test harnesses contain additional role usages that are test-only and out of production scope.
